transcript:
Header: 2026-05-27 11:00 PDT | Duration 56m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO), Maya (Head of ML), Evan (Infra), Liam (Product)

Summary (auto): 4 week POC, baseline end-to-end benchmark, cost model shared, SSO + SOC2 docs to go out.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick intros?
00:09 Alex: Alex here, CTO at Sundial. we run payments auth, tokenization, about 1200 txns/sec at peak during promos, avg day is 120 qps.
00:22 Maya: Maya, head of ML, I'll own the ML side, mainly inference for routing fraud models and nuances in prompts across countries.
00:35 Jordan: Great. Priya's our SE, she'll lead the bench plan and batching suggestions.
00:40 Priya: hi all, quick note: we typically focus on p95 and cold-start kv cache effects.
00:48 Liam: Product note — for checkout we have two paths: fast auth (short prompt, ~150 tokens output) and risk review (longer context, ~800 tokens)
01:05 Jordan: ok, success criteria? what does Sundial need to call this POC a win.
01:12 Alex: two things: 1) latency — p95 under 300ms for fast auth path; 2) predictability — a unit econ model that gets us to <$0.005 per auth call at our projected scale. plus security requirements (SAML SSO, audit logs).
01:35 Priya: noting that 150 token outputs with streaming vs non-streaming changes throughput. batching helps unit cost but increases latency. we'll simulate configurations.
01:46 Maya: can you remind me what Redwood's hosted model options are vs dedicated? we have regulatory windows where we need VPC connections.
01:55 Jordan: yes — hosted API fastest, but Dedicated or Private gives VPC/isolated network. for this POC we can run in a sandbox VPC so you can validate egress and network hops.
02:10 Evan: network wise we need to see TLS termination and whether we can pin to our NAT, also colocation of auth service times.
02:22 Jordan: we'll share a diagram.
02:28 Priya: about economics — I want to capture your workload shape. Alex said 1200 txns/sec peak — is that sustained or short promo spikes?
02:38 Alex: short spikes, maybe 30-90s bursts. baseline daily is 120 qps.
02:45 Priya: ok that implies we need to bench both steady-state and burst concurrency. we'll run bench scripts with ramp-ups and sudden bursts to exercise autoscaling and warm KV caches.
03:02 Liam: what's a KV cache warm-up look like?
03:06 Priya: typically prefix/KV cache warms after first N requests for the same customer session; for us keys are customer-id plus last 4 txns — warm-up can be sub-second if cache exists but first-time calls will have higher latency. we will measure cold vs warm p95.
03:25 Maya: cost baseline — what are typical per-token costs you model for the open models?
03:30 Jordan: for reference in our workbook we show per-1k-token render estimates across model families: about $0.40 to $2.00 per 1k output tokens depending on model size and quantization. for the short auth path (150 tokens) that's roughly $0.06 to $0.30 per call raw token cost before batching.
03:53 Alex: that's higher than we expected. we need <$0.005 per auth call — do you think batching helps that much?
04:00 Priya: batching can bring effective per-call cost down when you have many small requests in a batch. but for P95 latency requirements, there's a tradeoff: batching window adds queuing delay. we can also use prefix caching aggressively which often reduces token generation for repeated prompts.
04:20 Jordan: also quantized model variants and off-peak routing cut cost. we can route low-sensitivity requests to cheaper model tiers.
04:28 Evan: can you explain the queuing math? if we set a batching window of 10ms and target 1000 rps, what does that look like?
04:36 Priya: rough back-of-envelope: with 1000 rps, a 10ms window groups ~10 requests on average. if the model has per-batch overhead (kernel launch etc) then batching gives 10x token-efficiency for small outputs. but p95 also includes network + batch wait so we need to measure.
05:00 Liam: ok benchmarks — timeline and plan?
05:04 Priya: propose 4 week plan: week 0 (this week) collect traces and access, week 1 baseline single-client bench (functional + latency), week 2 scale up and burst tests with batching configs, week 3 caching and quantized variants comparison, week 4 finalize econ model and run final acceptance bench.
05:26 Alex: that timeline works. can we do parallel security review?
05:29 Jordan: yes, Jordan to send SOC2 summary, SSO guidance and onboarding checklist now.
05:36 Maya: what metrics will you report?
05:39 Priya: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, tokens per second, GPU utilization, effective cost per call, batching window stats, cold vs warm cache deltas, and end-to-end user-perceived latency.
05:56 Evan: also need trace ids to map our logs to Redwood traces for correlation.
06:02 Priya: we'll include trace hooks and link patterns.
06:07 Jordan: about cost modeling — we'll share a workbook that takes your traffic traces and runs scenarios: no-batch hosted, small-batch hosted, dedicated with 2x reserved GPUs, and private with quantized models.
06:22 Maya: examples of knobs?
06:24 Priya: batching window, max batch size, prefix cache TTL, KV cache size, quantization level (8-bit vs 4-bit), routing policy (cheapest-compatible, fallback), and autoscale buffer.
06:36 Alex: for budgeting — our finance team has a hard limit of $120k/month for inference. can you produce a scenario that hits that and tells us what throughput we can support and where to compromise?
06:50 Jordan: yes, we'll map to effective auth calls per month at your target SLO.
06:55 Liam: what about function/tool calls and streaming latencies? we don't use streaming much but might in future.
07:02 Priya: streaming affects both latency and token accounting; we'll include a small section in bench plan but not primary now.
07:10 Alex: security questions — do you have customer managed keys (KMS/HSM)? We need audit logs and retention controls.
07:18 Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer KMS and audit exports. for hosted we have encryption at rest and can plug into your KMS in dedicated/private options. we'll attach docs.
07:30 Maya: any gotchas we should expect in benching?
07:33 Priya: noisy neighbors on shared infra can skew results — we'll run multiple iterations and use p95/p99 and a warm cache baseline. also quantization sometimes yields small quality regressions — we will run a small eval set to measure generation drift.
07:53 Alex: quality regressions are acceptable up to an NPS delta? we want accuracy on fraud routing to not drop more than 0.5% FPR.
08:05 Priya: noted — we'll evaluate model variants on your eval set and surface regressions.
08:12 Jordan: sharing artifacts: we'll post a bench script link, cost workbook link, and security pack to the shared channel after the call.
08:22 Liam: timeline to decision?
08:25 Alex: if POC shows we can meet p95 and unit cost targets, we'll move to a 3 month pilot and plan for dedicated capacity buy. hoping to decide by end of Q3.
08:36 Jordan: great. last part — acceptance criteria recap.
08:39 Priya: A) p95 <300ms for auth path (warm cache), B) model/econ scenario that projects <$0.005 per auth call at target scale with acceptable tradeoffs, C) security checklist satisfied (SSO + audit logs), D) documented bench reproducible run.
09:02 Alex: agreed.
09:06 Jordan: ok action items recap — Jordan will email workbook and security docs; Maya/Evan to share traces and sandbox access; Priya to send bench plan.
09:20 Meeting ends.

Notes: occasional transcript errors: 'K V cache' sometimes transcribed as 'KVC ash', 'quantized' heard as 'quant eyes', product names slightly off. Links shared during call: https://redwood.example.com/bench-scripts (bench script + runbook), https://drive.example.com/sundial-trace-sample (placeholder), cost workbook link: https://sheets.example.com/redwood-sundial-cost-model
